findings.title: Non-null assertions on `fixAction` bypass the type system
findings.description: `fixRelPath` and `routeView` (line 143) use `finding.fixAction!` with no comment. The TypeScript rules treat assertions as a smell that needs a documented reason. The invariant is real: `fixableOf` filters on `f.fixable && f.fixAction`. But `fixRelPath` is exported and takes any `ConsistencyFinding`, so a caller that skips the filter gets a runtime crash. `gateByReadiness`, which is also exported, calls it too. Define a `FixableFinding = ConsistencyFinding & { fixAction: NonNullable<ConsistencyFinding['fixAction']> }` type guard. Use it for `fixableOf`, `routeView`, `gateByReadiness` and `fixRelPath`. The assertions then go away.

findings.title: Display flag `showWorktree` decides which fix report is printed
findings.description: `printCheckOutput` picks `printRoutedFixResult` over the legacy summary with `fixRes && showWorktree`. `showWorktree` is a presentation toggle, derived in `check.ts:165` from `projectViews.some(v => v.worktree !== undefined)`. It is also used as a proxy for "this result carries routed data" (`worktree` on log entries, `commits`, `deferred`). The two only agree because `buildAttributedViews` attaches worktrees only when there are two or more. If that rule changes, the output path changes without warning. Branch on the result itself, or pass an explicit `multiCheckout` argument.

findings.title: Scope/runCheck construction duplicated between CLI and MCP
findings.description: The `--slice` narrowing logic is copied into `packages/mcp-server/src/tools/workflowTools.ts`. Both build `scopeViews` with `fileSlice: \`${n}-slice\`` and pick `checker.check` or `checker.checkAll`. Both also wrap `resolveInvokingCheckout` in similar try/catch error translation. The fix-mode plan-then-apply sequence is duplicated too. The previous code already had this duplication, and this change was a chance to remove it. A shared core helper, for example `scopeViewsToSlice(views, index)`, would stop the two consumers drifting. Their parity is currently enforced only by tests.

findings.title: `checker.fix` and `checker.fixAll` are now unused in production code
findings.description: Neither the CLI nor the MCP tool calls `fix` or `fixAll` any more. Only tests do. They are also the unrouted, per-view-write path, which is the one this slice replaced. If they are not a deliberate public API, remove them or mark them deprecated. Otherwise a future caller may use them and skip ownership routing.

findings.title: `workflow.auto_fix` now commits into other checkouts without a prompt
findings.description: Previously an all-slices fix prompted whenever `--yes` was absent, including when `auto_fix` was the trigger. Now only an explicit `--fix` prompts. Plain `cf check` with `auto_fix` writes and commits in non-invoking worktrees silently. The comment cites slice 213 SC 11, so this appears to be a deliberate design decision. Make sure the README and CHANGELOG say plainly that `auto_fix` can create commits in sibling worktrees.

findings.title: Slice index is parsed from a user-visible description string
findings.description: This is moved code, not new code. It groups findings by regex-matching `[175]` at the start of `description`. That conflicts with the project rule against using user-visible labels as logical structure. `fixAction.subjectIndex` now exists for fixable findings. A structured `sliceIndex` on `ConsistencyFinding` would fix the problem properly.

findings.title: Test file exports helpers and defines a function that reads module state
findings.description: This file exports `designPath`, `tasksPath`, `completeBeta`, `worktreeCtx`, `createRoutedSetup`, `dryRun` and `aboutSubject`. A grep found no importer of the test file. The exports are unused and make the file look like a shared helper module. `createProjectFor` sits at the bottom of the file and reads the module-level `setup` variable. Drop the `export` keywords, or move the helpers into `tests/helpers/`. Make `createProjectFor` take its base project as an argument.

findings.title: Fix routing, readiness gating and commit rollback are covered with real git
findings.description: The tests use real git worktrees through `gitWorktreeFixture`. They cover owner and non-owner routing, overlapping ranges, an owner that lacks the file, and dirty, busy, detached and missing checkouts. They also cover a dirty target between plan and apply, staged-file isolation, and a rejecting pre-commit hook followed by restore. The case where restore also fails is covered as well. A passthrough spy asserts that the single-checkout path runs no git. Exception handling in `checkoutReadiness.ts` and `routedFixes.ts` follows the project rules: each catch is specific, commented, and either logged or converted into an explicit `DeferReason` or `fixErrors` entry. Nothing is swallowed silently.

structured_findings.summary: Non-null assertions on `fixAction` bypass the type system
Display flag `showWorktree` decides which fix report is printed
Scope/runCheck construction duplicated between CLI and MCP
`checker.fix` and `checker.fixAll` are now unused in production code
`workflow.auto_fix` now commits into other checkouts without a prompt
Slice index is parsed from a user-visible description string
Test file exports helpers and defines a function that reads module state
Fix routing, readiness gating and commit rollback are covered with real git
